correctness.rationale: The stronger nilpotent-sampling theorem uses exact square-zero cone cardinalities, Borel intersections (odd characteristic), and the projection bijection onto the Heisenberg quotient (even characteristic), proving sampling invariance and the absence of two-dimensional nilpotent-generated subalgebras. For odd characteristic, a trace-invariance argument makes every two-dimensional proper Lie subalgebra a Borel; eigenline incidences give the exact one-/two-/zero-Borel event unions. Characteristic two reduces to a nondegenerate central commutator pairing on a two-dimensional quotient. The all-length formulas and geometric-series waiting times follow exactly. Independent exhaustive GF(2), GF(3), GF(4), GF(5), GF(7) checks agree.

value.rationale: Uniform sampling on the quadratic nilpotent cone is a natural restricted-generator model motivated by prior nilpotent-generation problems. The exact invariance of full-generation probabilities despite elimination of every intermediate two-dimensional outcome is an unexpected, structurally explained effect. The exact fixed-first-generator probability is a natural quantitative form of 3/2-generation: it measures how frequently a prescribed matrix can be completed into a generating system. Three sharply different odd-characteristic decay laws, an even-characteristic central obstruction, and exact waiting times form an all-field structural classification not supplied by the unrestricted rank-two probability.
